>  	real_t radial_distance = (p_origin - (p_current_origin + bone_axis * lam)).length();

This equation can be made easier to parse if you break out the factors onto separate lines, but these factors don't necessarily deserve to have their own descriptive names.

But regardless this is a variable and should be named in a way that makes reading the code easy

You're right.  The standard practice in geometric equations when they are being explained is to use single letters to represent the points and factors rather than these long variable names.  See for example: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyperbola#As_locus_of_points

What they do is introduce each component as a single letter with a description, and then render the structure of the equations clear and easy to see by using those single letters.  Attempting to merge a simple symbol and its description into a single unit is doomed to fail.

I do not think this type of compatibility breakage is allowed.

```
The following changes are acceptable in minor releases, but not patch releases:
...
    Deprecating a method, member variable, or class. This is done by adding a deprecated flag to its class reference, which will show up in the editor. When a method is marked as deprecated, it's slated to be removed in the next major release.
...
The following changes are considered compatibility-breaking and can only be performed in a new major release:
    Renaming or removing a method, member variable, or class.
```
The correct way is to keep the existing `inside` member and `is_/set_` methods, and add `deprecated="true"` into the documentation XML.
